identified_defects: V2 conflates missing vendor artifacts and expected parameters with an irreducible semantic blocker even though the field relationship and required read-only operation are identifiable.
The source log-clear instruction would remove diagnostic evidence and is not part of the offset validation.
changes.objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 preserves V2's prohibition on guessed PMBus access while replacing the permanent BLOCKED label with explicit prerequisite, ownership, safe pre-collection, prohibited-action, and closure criteria. The agent can now collect identity evidence without falsely claiming that the offset was validated.
resolved_blockers: The missing vendor document and decoder no longer create a permanent automation-classification blocker.
remaining_blockers: Execution remains gated until the applicable field map, expected value, and read-only tool are supplied and matched to the detected CRPS.

revision_candidate.test_name: CRPS Latch-on-Fault Offset to Next Configuration Block
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify that the CRPS latch-on-fault configuration field contains the vendor-defined byte offset from the current configuration block to the next block.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the CRPS model and firmware revision covered by the supplied vendor PMBus configuration-block specification.
revision_candidate.target_scope: The identified CRPS slot and the single vendor-defined offset field; do not apply the expected value to other PSU models or firmware families.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: CRPS identity and slot, firmware/VPD revision, applicable vendor specification, field address, block boundaries, byte order/encoding, expected offset, and approved read-only decoder or command.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Run the vendor-approved read-only configuration-block decode for the identified CRPS and capture the raw field and decoded byte offset. Do not substitute a generic PMBus scan.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Confirm the specification-to-CRPS identity match, management access path, tool compatibility, and non-writing mode. Preserve existing logs.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: CRPS identity/firmware, tool and specification version, raw field bytes, decoded offset, current and next block boundaries, byte order, and timestamped read output.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The expected offset and encoding in the applicable vendor PMBus Application Note or Firmware Specification. The end user performs the final comparison.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Read-only access only. No blind bus scan, configuration write, PSU reset, firmware operation, or log clearing.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: The platform/PSU engineer must approve the specification, detected target, and resolved read-only command before access.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The engineer supplies proprietary artifacts and confirms applicability; the agent may collect the approved readback and evidence.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: If the management path becomes unavailable, stop, preserve error/SEL evidence, and follow the approved BMC/PSU access recovery procedure without writing or resetting the PSU.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Stop if the CRPS identity, specification applicability, field map, expected value, read-only property, or management target cannot be confirmed.

identified_defects: V2 over-classified missing vendor artifacts and approval gates as BLOCKED.
DeepSeek's sensor grep is insufficient evidence for five firmware transitions and can omit relevant raw PSU data.
The source instruction to clear logs would destroy baseline evidence.
changes.objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 keeps V2's firmware safety controls and five-cycle scope but correctly classifies the activity as technically executable with supplied vendor inputs. It also distinguishes safe baseline collection from the prohibited flash and defines per-cycle completion evidence.
resolved_blockers: Missing images, command, and approval are represented as readiness gates rather than a permanent classification blocker.
remaining_blockers: Execution cannot start until the exact images, target map, sequence, power constraints, and recovery plan are supplied and approved.

revision_candidate.test_name: PSU Firmware N/N-1 Upgrade and Downgrade, Five Cycles
revision_candidate.purpose: Perform five approved PSU firmware N/N-1 transition cycles through the BMC HPM path and verify firmware activation, PSU health, BMC recovery, and SUT power-cycle recovery after each required transition.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the PSU model, BMC/HPM implementation, and firmware family covered by the supplied compatibility statement and recovery procedure.
revision_candidate.target_scope: The engineer-identified PSU slot or PSU set for each transition; record whether redundant PSUs are updated sequentially or together.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Exact PSU identity/current version, signed N/N-1 images and hashes, vendor HPM method, five-cycle order/timing, maintenance approval, redundancy plan, OOB/KVM access, and recovery/replacement path.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Use only the vendor-approved HPM flash procedure for the resolved target and image. Execute the defined N/N-1 order for five cycles, collecting firmware and health evidence after every transition. Do not substitute a version query for the flash test.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Dedicated maintenance window, evacuated workloads, stable redundant power where required, verified image compatibility, captured baseline, and tested recovery access.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Per-cycle image/hash/target, flash status and timing, activated version, BMC reconnect, PSU sensors and output state, SEL/host delta, SUT boot and power-cycle recovery, and final firmware state.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The approved vendor compatibility/update procedure plus the source requirement for five N/N-1 cycles and successful SUT power-cycle recovery.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never infer the PSU target or image. Preserve logs. Stop on output loss, image mismatch, abnormal redundancy, management loss, flash error, or incomplete recovery.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Explicit approval is required before the firmware sequence and again if the target, image, order, or recovery plan changes.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: An engineer supplies/approves proprietary images and the vendor procedure and may operate a WebUI-only step; the agent may collect read-only pre/post evidence and follow an approved automatable interface.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop subsequent cycles, preserve evidence, use the vendor recovery/reflash or PSU replacement procedure through OOB/KVM/local access, and verify stable redundant power and SUT recovery before resuming.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Any unresolved identity, compatibility, sequence, approval, redundancy, active-workload, OOB, flash, power-output, or recovery condition.

revision_candidate.purpose: After the source owner confirms that both activities are intended, install the approved OS on the dedicated target with the specified TPM BIOS state and verify the installed OS exposes the required TPM function.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The identified SUT, BIOS/TPM implementation, approved OS image, boot mode, and dedicated disposable installation target.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Only the engineer-designated installation disk and named TPM control; all other storage and security state are out of scope.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Corrected source requirement, OS image/hash, target disk, boot mode, exact TPM start/end state, Secure Boot/key policy, installer/driver inputs, TPM verification method, backup, and recovery plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: An operator performs or approves the BIOS and installer steps on the confirmed target. After installation, collect the approved TPM device, capability, kernel, and OS evidence. Do not substitute post-install inventory for the required installation and state transition.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Resolve the source conflict, isolate the dedicated target, protect keys/data, capture before-state evidence, and verify OOB/reimage recovery.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Corrected intent, image/target identity, before/after TPM BIOS state, installer result, OS identity, TPM device and capability evidence, target-only storage changes, boot health, and preserved BMC/host logs.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The corrected testcase requirement plus the applicable platform TPM/BIOS and OS validation specification.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never guess a disk or TPM action. Do not clear TPM, alter keys, or change Secure Boot unless explicitly required and recoverable. Preserve logs.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Engineer decision on intent, then explicit approval for the resolved disk, BIOS/security transition, installation, and reboot.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: BIOS and interactive installer operations may require an operator; post-install evidence collection can be automated.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Restore the approved BIOS/security state or reimage only the designated target; preserve keys and non-target storage; use OOB access if boot fails.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved source purpose, unidentified target, ambiguous TPM transition, unavailable backup/recovery, unapproved key impact, or any non-target storage risk.

identified_defects: V2 over-classifies a physical/manual boundary as BLOCKED.

revision_candidate.test_name: Serial Port Bidirectional Communication Check
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify bidirectional communication over the designated SUT serial port using the approved cable, client endpoint, serial settings, and harmless test payload.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The identified board/serial interface and client whose electrical standard and pinout are documented as compatible.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Only the named SUT serial port and client endpoint; do not substitute a different console or network path.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Port map, RS-232/RS-422/RS-485 or other standard, pinout, cable, baud/data/parity/stop/flow settings, client role, payload, expected response, timeout/retry, operator, and alternate console.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: The operator connects the approved cable, configures both endpoints, sends the approved payload, records the complete transmit/receive transcript, and disconnects or restores the original console state.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Verify electrical and pin compatibility, confirm the link is not an active production console, and ensure alternate/OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Connection record, endpoint/settings table, exact payload and response, timestamped transcript, observed errors/timeouts, and post-test console/system health.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The platform serial-interface specification and the owner-defined expected response for the approved payload.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No unknown cable, voltage standard, pinout, peer, or arbitrary terminal command. Preserve logs and stop on unexpected output or console impact.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: The platform owner approves the resolved link definition; the operator approves and performs the physical connection and terminal interaction.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Cable handling, terminal observation, and the physical acceptance criterion are manual. The agent may organize supplied transcript and supporting health logs only.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Terminate the session, restore the original cable/console state, use OOB access if the serial console is lost, and verify BMC/SUT health.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Missing or mismatched electrical/pinout data, unknown console ownership, absent expected response, framing/electrical errors, unexpected peer behavior, or unavailable alternate console.

identified_defects: The source procedure and criteria disagree on BIOS acceptance scope.
DeepSeek includes ip link, which is not evidence of USB detection.
V2 over-classifies a hybrid manual-plus-automated workflow as BLOCKED.
changes.objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 preserves V2's device-safety and coverage warnings but correctly classifies the test as a hybrid workflow, exposes the BIOS-versus-OS source conflict, and defines per-port completion evidence without claiming one lsusb snapshot is sufficient.
resolved_blockers: Manual attachment and missing matrix are treated as execution prerequisites instead of permanent non-automability.
remaining_blockers: Execution waits for the corrected BIOS/OS criterion and exact port/device matrix.

revision_candidate.test_name: All USB Port Device Detection in BIOS and OS
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify each required physical USB port detects the approved known-good device in BIOS and the installed OS, with complete port-by-port coverage.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The identified platform revision, BIOS/BMC/OS, USB controller topology, and approved test-device/driver matrix.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Every port in the supplied matrix, including front, rear, and internal ports as applicable; map each port to its controller/hub path.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Port/controller map, device identity and power/driver requirements, BIOS/KVM evidence method, definition of detected/usable, operator sequence, usbutils, and recovery plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: For each matrix row, the operator connects the approved device and records BIOS detection when required. After OS boot, collect complete lsusb output, USB topology, device/driver details, and kernel enumeration evidence for that placement.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Approve the device, confirm no boot/security/storage risk, capture baseline topology/logs, and ensure OOB/alternate-console access.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Completed coverage matrix with port/device identity, BIOS capture, OS enumeration/topology/driver evidence, kernel timestamps/errors, and restored final state.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The corrected BIOS/OS acceptance statement and platform USB port/device matrix. The engineer decides whether enumeration alone or usable operation is required.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No arbitrary or sensitive USB media, no unexpected mounts, no log clearing, and no coverage claim without per-port evidence.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Approve the matrix/device and every physical attachment sequence; an operator performs placement and BIOS observation.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Physical attachment/movement and BIOS visual evidence are manual; OS enumeration and logs are automatable after each placement.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Safely remove the device, unmount if explicitly permitted and required, restore boot/input/security state, and use OOB access if console or boot is affected.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unknown port/device identity, unexpected mount or boot behavior, over-current/power error, controller reset, security impact, incomplete coverage, or unresolved BIOS/OS acceptance conflict.

identified_defects: DeepSeek changes both the worker selection and duration and returns only a tail, so it does not execute or evidence the source test.
The source asks to clear dmesg, which destroys baseline evidence.
V2 does not explicitly distinguish a short sanity run from completion of the eight-hour request.

remaining_blockers: Execution waits for worker/topology intent, thresholds, package, maintenance, and recovery approval.

revision_candidate.test_name: Eight-Hour CPU Stress with 225 stress-ng Workers
revision_candidate.purpose: Run 225 stress-ng CPU workers for eight hours on the approved SUT and verify the system remains workable without unexpected platform errors.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Linux SUT with the detected CPU topology, approved stress-ng build, adequate cooling/power, dedicated maintenance window, and OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: The SUT CPU complex; 225 workers and eight hours are fixed source parameters unless the testcase owner formally revises the source.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Worker/topology approval, stress-ng version/package, maintenance window, workload evacuation, stop thresholds, monitoring sources, workable/recovery checks, and OOB/KVM plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Run `stress-ng --cpu 225 -t 8h` on the SUT after an evidence-preserving baseline. Capture complete output and health telemetry; do not substitute `--cpu 0 --timeout 600s`.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Approved package, idle/dedicated SUT, confirmed cooling/power margin, baseline logs/telemetry, tested stop command, and OOB access.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Topology and approval, full stress-ng output/exit status, eight-hour timestamps, continuous thermal/power/frequency/throttle data, kernel/MCE/EDAC and BMC/SEL deltas, remaining process check, and post-run management/workload recovery.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The source's 225-worker/eight-hour requirement and engineer-supplied platform health/error/thermal/power thresholds.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No log clearing, no unapproved package or parameter change, and no active production workload. Stop on approved thermal/current/power, error, hang, or management-loss thresholds.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Explicit approval is required before package installation and before starting the eight-hour high-load run.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The engineer supplies topology/threshold decisions and approves the window; execution and evidence collection can then be automated.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop all stress workers, preserve evidence, use OOB/KVM on management loss, verify normal thermal/power state and process termination, and do not retry without review.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unapproved worker oversubscription, inadequate cooling/power, active users/jobs, abnormal baseline, thermal/power/throttle limit, kernel/MCE/EDAC/BMC error, hang, management loss, or incomplete evidence.

identified_defects: The source assigns different values to two documented aliases for the same virtual-memory worker option, so an execution agent cannot know whether 15 or 9 is authoritative.
The source asks to clear logs and thereby destroys comparison evidence.
The source's `badblock` phrase is not a defined host-RAM metric.
DeepSeek loses the exact eight-hour, 90%, and worker-count intent by substituting a generic memory-allocation description.
changes.objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 uses the official upstream manual to prove that the two source options are aliases with conflicting values, changes the primary outcome to REWRITE_REQUIRED, and supplies a corrected single-option command form without inventing the missing worker count. It preserves the eight-hour duration, 90% host-memory intent, and all V2 safety gates.
resolved_blockers: The tool/package requirement and high-risk nature are treated as resolvable readiness conditions, not a permanent automation blocker.
remaining_blockers: Execution remains prohibited until the worker-count conflict, allocation behavior, acceptance definitions, capacity, approval, and recovery plan are resolved.

revision_candidate.test_name: Eight-Hour Host Memory Stress with stress-ng
revision_candidate.purpose: Run the engineer-approved stress-ng virtual-memory workload at the source-required 90% memory target for eight hours and verify host-memory and platform health.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Approved Linux server SUT with host DDR memory, a validated stress-ng version, sufficient cooling/power margin, and OOB recovery. This case does not test GPU HBM.
revision_candidate.target_scope: All host-memory resources intentionally covered by the approved virtual-memory workers; the source's conflicting 15-versus-9 worker count must be resolved before execution.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: One approved worker count, verified `--vm-bytes 90%` semantics for the installed version, DIMM/NUMA/swap/cgroup inventory, memory-error acceptance definition, maintenance approval, monitoring limits, stop thresholds, and recovery owner.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: After preserving a baseline, run `stress-ng --vm <APPROVED_WORKER_COUNT> --vm-bytes 90% --timeout 8h` using exactly one approved virtual-memory worker option. Do not execute the conflicting source command unchanged or substitute DeepSeek's generic `--mem-alloc/all` description.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Approved package and corrected command, dedicated/idle SUT, capacity and allocation-risk review, baseline ECC/EDAC/MCE/kernel/BMC/SEL evidence, tested abort command, and working OOB/KVM access.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Owner-approved command and version semantics, DIMM/NUMA/memory/swap baseline, full eight-hour stress-ng output and exit status, allocation/swap/OOM and thermal/power telemetry, ECC/EDAC/MCE/kernel/BMC/SEL deltas, process termination, and post-run manageability/workload recovery.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The source's eight-hour and 90% memory-stress intent plus engineer-supplied worker count, `badblock` evidence mapping, acceptable error thresholds, and workable/recovery criteria.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never clear evidence logs or guess duplicate-option precedence. Do not run on an active service host or exceed approved allocation, OOM, swap, thermal, power, ECC, or management thresholds.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Explicit approval is required for package installation, the corrected command, maintenance window, high-memory workload, stop thresholds, and recovery plan.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Engineering must resolve command and acceptance semantics; after approval, workload control and evidence collection can be automated while final platform judgment remains with the engineer.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop all stress-ng workers, preserve evidence, use OOB/KVM if the host becomes unresponsive, verify memory pressure and swap normalize, confirm no worker remains, and do not retry until abnormal events are reviewed.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved worker count or allocation semantics, unsafe available capacity, active workloads, abnormal baseline, OOM or swap storm, new uncorrectable/corrected errors beyond the approved threshold, kernel/BMC fault, thermal/power breach, hang, management loss, or incomplete evidence.

identified_defects: DeepSeek reduces five required observation paths to one out-of-band IPMI line.
The source contains literal credentials and disables TLS verification, which must not be copied into execution or evidence.
The source assumes a vendor-specific Redfish Manager identifier and IPMI cipher suite.
V2 incorrectly treats BIOS and web-UI evidence as optional supplemental evidence.
changes.objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 reverses V2's scope reduction by retaining BIOS and BMC-web observations, reclassifies the resulting hybrid workflow, and replaces unsafe hard-coded endpoint/credential/TLS assumptions with explicit platform inputs while preserving safe automated IPMI/Redfish collection.
resolved_blockers: Missing tools, credentials, endpoint, and expected baseline are provisionable readiness items, not evidence that version collection is technically impossible.
remaining_blockers: Final execution/decision waits for expected-version mapping, authorized access, and the approved BIOS/web evidence method.

revision_candidate.test_name: BMC Firmware Version Cross-Interface Verification
revision_candidate.purpose: Confirm that the approved BMC firmware revision is reported consistently by BIOS Server Management, in-band IPMI, out-of-band IPMI, the BMC web UI, and Redfish.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The identified server and BMC with authorized host, management-network, browser/KVM, and Redfish access. Manager URI, certificate policy, IPMI cipher, and UI paths are platform-specific.
revision_candidate.target_scope: One verified SUT/BMC instance across all five source-required interfaces; do not substitute a different management controller or reduce the check to one CLI path.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Expected BMC version, permitted display normalization, BMC identity/address, protected credentials, TLS trust policy, Redfish Manager URI or discovery access, supported IPMI settings, UI/KVM method, and BIOS-access approval/window.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Collect in-band and out-of-band `ipmitool mc info`; discover the target under `/redfish/v1/Managers` and read its `FirmwareVersion`; collect the BMC-web and BIOS Server Management version displays through approved browser/KVM or manual evidence. Compare every value with the baseline and each other.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Verified SUT/BMC identity, authorized least-privilege read access, approved tools and secret mechanism, trusted or explicitly excepted lab TLS path, expected-version baseline, and approved BIOS/UI access method.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Expected version and normalization rule; redacted timestamped IPMI outputs; Redfish Manager URI, identity, and FirmwareVersion; BIOS and web-UI screen evidence; cross-path comparison; and before/after unexpected-log delta without clearing history.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Platform firmware recipe or release baseline supplied by the firmware owner. DMTF Manager FirmwareVersion defines the Redfish value but does not supply the platform's expected revision.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Read-only queries only. Never embed or log credentials, contact an unverified endpoint, clear logs, reset/update the BMC, change power state, or reboot for BIOS evidence without approval.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Owner confirmation of the expected version and mapping is required for PASS/FAIL; authorization is required for credentials and any reboot/interactive BIOS access.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: IPMI/Redfish collection and comparison are automatable. BIOS and BMC-web observations remain manual unless an approved KVM/browser automation path captures equivalent evidence.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop on endpoint/authentication/certificate mismatch, preserve redacted evidence, exit UI/KVM without saving changes, and return the host to its prior boot state if an approved BIOS reboot was used.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unverified target, exposed credentials, failed authentication, unapproved TLS exception/cipher/reboot, missing required path, version disagreement without an approved mapping, or inability to preserve redacted evidence.

identified_defects: The source conflates named ACPI table existence with appearance of a table name in dmesg.
The source gives no platform-specific required/conditional table matrix.
DeepSeek's SSH example exposes a password and disables host-key verification.
Neither source nor V2 explicitly excludes false claims of end-to-end RAS functionality from a static table-presence check.
changes.objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 preserves V2's safe automated collection but corrects the semantic boundary: a sysfs table, a kernel message, and proven RAS behavior are different claims. It also makes architecture-specific applicability and no-false-completion explicit.
resolved_blockers: Missing acpica-tools is not a blocker when sysfs and kernel-log evidence are sufficient; the package is optional for a deeper dump.

revision_candidate.test_name: OS Exposure of Expected ACPI BERT, ERST, and HEST Tables
revision_candidate.purpose: Confirm that each ACPI error-record table required for the exact platform is exposed by firmware and recognized by the running OS without unexpected APEI initialization errors.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The identified server architecture, BIOS/firmware build, OS/kernel, and enabled RAS configuration. Table requirements are architecture- and platform-specific.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Firmware-provided BERT, ERST, and HEST tables and their OS/kernel exposure only; no hardware error injection or persistence/recovery function is exercised.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Platform identity and architecture, BIOS/firmware and kernel versions, RAS configuration, required/conditional/not-applicable table matrix, and acceptance rule for table validity and kernel recognition.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Using authorized read-only access, list the exact BERT/ERST/HEST entries in `/sys/firmware/acpi/tables`, capture safe metadata or approved raw dumps, and collect full contextual ACPI/APEI kernel messages. Record command status and distinguish absent, inaccessible, invalid, and not-applicable results.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Verified SUT/OS identity, readable kernel logs and ACPI table path, protected remote access, preserved log history, and the platform expectation matrix for final judgment.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Identity/version baseline, expected-table matrix, table names/sizes/hashes/headers or approved dumps, contextual dmesg/journal output, permission and command status, unexpected ACPI errors, and per-table comparison result.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact platform's firmware/RAS specification. ACPI defines BERT, HEST, and ERST mechanisms but does not require the same table set on every server configuration.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Read-only inspection only; do not clear logs, write firmware/ACPI state, inject errors, use unverified SSH endpoints, expose credentials, or claim end-to-end RAS validation.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: No approval is needed for authorized read-only collection; the platform owner must provide the expectation matrix and adjudicate unexplained absence or initialization errors.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Collection, parsing, and matrix comparison are automatable. Platform applicability and final interpretation of unexpected firmware/kernel behavior remain engineering decisions.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No device-state recovery is expected. On access/identity/permission anomalies, stop, preserve the outputs, and request corrected access or platform mapping.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: SUT identity mismatch, unprotected credentials, unavailable read-only evidence, command/permission failure that obscures presence, missing expectation matrix for final judgment, or evidence of an unexpected ACPI/APEI initialization error requiring owner review.

identified_defects: The source procedure never specifies the error-injection stimulus required by the Item and Criteria.
The all-channel second-DIMM target is not mapped to actual slot/channel identifiers.
Register behavior, event type/count, and host/BMC acceptance fields are undefined.
V2 classifies the complete case as MANUAL ONLY even though evidence collection and correlation form a meaningful automated phase.

It does not relax V2's operator, isolation, bounded-event, or recovery gates.
resolved_blockers: Manual setup and injection do not make the whole case MANUAL ONLY; automated read-only collection and correlation are retained as a valid phase.
remaining_blockers: No state-changing execution may begin until the platform-specific injection SOP, map, expected behavior, limits, approval, and recovery are complete.

revision_candidate.test_name: Second-DIMM Memory RAS Injection Across Approved Channels
revision_candidate.purpose: For each owner-mapped second-DIMM target, perform a bounded approved ECC/RAS injection and verify the expected leaky-bucket/register behavior and correlated host and BMC SEL reporting.

revision_candidate.test_name: Cycle BMC Test-File Upload and Removal at 40 C and -5% Rails
revision_candidate.purpose: Exercise the approved BMC transfer/storage path for one owner-selected finite cycle count or 30-minute campaign under physical margin, verifying every object's integrity through an owner-approved end-to-end method, exact deletion, continuous capacity reserve and management health.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Exact BMC firmware/interface/storage partition in calibrated 40 C and owner-named -5% 5 V/3.3 V rail conditions, with signed control/measurement points, tolerances, soak and restoration sequence.
revision_candidate.target_scope: One canonical owner-created sandbox root and one uniquely named non-sensitive object per cycle; containment is revalidated before each delete. Never firmware partitions, configuration, logs, certificates, symlink/reparse escapes or arbitrary BMC paths.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Supported interface/commands; canonical sandbox identity and containment check; non-sensitive file size/hash and immutable per-cycle object naming; one trustworthy end-to-end integrity method for every cycle (server checksum, authenticated readback plus local hash comparison, or owner-approved equivalent); one authoritative bound (fixed count or 30 minutes), including in-progress-cycle timeout behavior; free-space floor and sampling cadence; exact margined rails/control points/tolerances/soak/restore; transfer timeout/retry policy, expected SEL/log behavior, cleanup and recovery approval.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Read-only BMC/storage baseline may occur now. After specification, operator establishes and independently verifies the signed margin. The authenticated client uploads the uniquely identified object, proves end-to-end integrity through the mandatory approved method, revalidates canonical containment, removes only that object, proves absence and records free space every cycle. Execute only the selected finite bound; do not choose between count and time at runtime.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Sandbox/privilege scope and canonical containment are proven, OOB remains reachable, continuous environment and per-cycle capacity monitoring are ready.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Firmware/interface/partition identity; canonical sandbox and per-cycle object identity/name/size/hash; chosen loop rule and boundary behavior; exact per-cycle upload/integrity/containment/delete/absence results and timestamps; per-cycle free space plus minimum observed reserve; completed count or full duration; continuous temperature and named-rail traces with tolerances; BMC services/sensors/SEL/network; final capacity, no residual object and nominal restoration.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Every cycle required by the selected bound completes with matching integrity and exact cleanup, measured reserve never crosses its floor, signed environmental tolerances hold continuously, and BMC services/SEL meet owner criteria.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not browse/write arbitrary BMC paths, follow symlink/path traversal outside the sandbox, upload firmware/config/secret data, clear SEL, select or change the loop rule, retry automatically, run unboundedly or delete by wildcard/uncertain identity.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: BMC owner supplies sandbox/object/bound method; lab operator controls named physical rails, temperature and recovery.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Environment is manual; the owner-defined bounded transfer loop can be automated only through the approved interface.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop new transfers, preserve the failed exact object/evidence, restore named rails/temperature by the signed sequence, use supported cleanup/service recovery and never delete an uncertain path.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved canonical target/method/bound/margin, unavailable or failed trustworthy end-to-end integrity method, containment failure, capacity floor breach, integrity or deletion failure, BMC service loss, SEL/storage/power/thermal anomaly, fixture drift or monitoring gap.

revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On rejection/POST failure preserve task/logs and use approved recovery or return to known-good BIOS.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Missing or unordered per-hop manifest/approval, unsupported target/path, anti-rollback rejection, any hop's signature/component/compatibility mismatch, power/task error, failed activation/version, lost keys/settings, POST/boot/device regression or no recovery.

identified_defects: Generic Redfish substitution changes OEM method.
CPLD component/activation unspecified.

remaining_blockers: OEM image/component/activation/recovery.

revision_candidate.test_name: Flash the Designated CPLD Through the BMC OEM Path
revision_candidate.purpose: Update one explicitly mapped CPLD component with its signed image and prove correct version, required activation and platform power/management/device health.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Exact board assembly/CPLD hardware revision/BMC OEM updater combination.
revision_candidate.target_scope: One named CPLD at a physical board/location and component inventory ID; other CPLDs, BMC and BIOS excluded.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Board/CPLD identity and current/target version, image hash/signature/compatibility, OEM SOP/endpoint, dependency/update order, preserve-setting meaning, activation reset/DC/AC cycle, stable power, rollback/recovery and approval.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Capture component/board/power baseline, verify image, use only OEM path, monitor complete task, perform only signed activation sequence, then query the same component and validate affected buses/devices.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Alternate management/power recovery and correct board/component map proven.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Physical/component mapping; image/hash; pre/post CPLD version from authoritative source; exact OEM task/messages; activation/power trace; BMC/host/PCIe/I2C/sensor/SEL health appropriate to affected CPLD.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Named CPLD reaches target version and all dependent platform paths recover; a generic firmware inventory version is insufficient.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No generic standard endpoint assumption, wrong CPLD/image/order, power interruption outside activation, automatic retry or unrelated firmware flash.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: CPLD/platform owner approves component, image, activation and recovery.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: OEM UI/power activation or recovery may be manual.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On task/activation failure preserve state and use board-specific CPLD recovery; do not repeat blindly.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Component ambiguity, incompatible/signature-failed image, unsupported OEM path, dependency/power issue, task error, lost management or affected-bus/device failure.

revision_candidate.required_inputs: Spec title/revision, BD1 mapping, intended action, data ownership, commands/manual steps, duration/iterations, evidence, safety, measurable acceptance and recovery.
